A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DEX research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original language-modeling, retrieval, in-context learning, instruction-tuning and ablation results, including experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports HumanEval, Math500 and latency results.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Figure 9 retain the same output-subtraction operation, selective head adaptation, lambda annealing and updated parameters. Instruction-tuning applications were already present in v2 Appendix C.

E1.justification: v3 Section 4.4 expands instruction-tuning evaluation from six to eight benchmarks by adding HumanEval and Math500, extending existing coding and mathematics coverage. OpenHermes training data and the other evaluated datasets and tasks are retained.

E2.justification: v2 Table 7 and v3 Table 4 retain the same instruction-tuned Base/LoRA/FT/DEX and pretrained LoRA/DEX comparisons. Comparator membership in the other experiments is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Figure 12 adds latency as an inference-efficiency metric, reported across context lengths alongside throughput. Previously stated training budgets, model configurations and retrieval/in-context learning procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The efficiency analysis adds evidence about latency scaling with context length in Figure 12b, supplementing the earlier throughput-only study. Head-selection, lambda, training-data-size, redundancy and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The throughput reporting still averages 30 batches after five warm-up batches. No new repeated-run or seed information, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: The instruction-tuning table adds HumanEval and Math500 scores and recomputes averages over eight benchmarks, so those averages are not directly comparable with v2's six-benchmark averages. Pretrained+DEX's AGIEval score changes from 37.8 to 37.9. Figure 12 adds latency results; other matched results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 retain the same mathematical content. The effective-attention pseudoinverse derivation, optimization approximation and associated assumptions are unchanged between v2 Appendix F.3 and v3 Appendix E.3.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the three proposed explanations for DIFF's success and the claim that DEX efficiently transfers its benefits to pretrained models. The expanded conclusion restates these existing contributions.

C2.justification: v3 omits v2 Appendix C's attention-focus explanation for IFEval/GSM8K gains and its attribution of AGIEval gains primarily to additional training. It adds an explicit diminishing-returns interpretation of Figure 13. The substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The data recipes, training hyperparameters, model configuration, hardware/software information and data/checkpoint links are retained. Implementation Details moves from Appendix F to Appendix E without substantive changes to reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v3 adds Chen et al., Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code, as reference 14 for HumanEval. The other cited works and the substantive related-work positioning are retained.

P1.justification: Instruction tuning moves from Appendix C into Section 4.4 with condensed prose. The conclusion is expanded, and affiliations, conference text and acknowledgments are updated. Most other prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The instruction-tuning table moves into the main text and widens to accommodate two additional benchmarks. Figure 12 becomes a two-panel throughput/latency display. Existing plots are retained, with localized layout changes and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The added HumanEval/Math500 comparisons and latency curve modestly broaden evidence for DEX's utility and efficiency, while moving instruction tuning into the main text improves its visibility. Some task-specific interpretation is removed, but the existing analyses and reproducibility information are retained, supporting a limited net improvement.
